input.quote: SFJ shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain from each Third Party contractor that SFJ or its Affiliate proposes to engage to conduct activities under or in connection with this Agreement on behalf of SFJ or its Affiliates (i) an assignment, (ii) an exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers, or (iii) a non‑exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers ((i) through (iii) in order of preference), to PB of any Trial Invention
input.rationale: There is no inbound licence to us that is revocable or scope-limited: this Co-Development Agreement gives PB (our party) rights to the relevant IP by ownership rather than licence — PB retains all Existing PB Intellectual Property (11.1.1.1), is the exclusive owner of all Trial Inventions with SFJ assigning and causing its Affiliates and Permitted Third Parties to assign (11.1.1.3(a)-(b)), and acquires sole ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results (11.1.1.4). Where assignment cannot be obtained from SFJ's consultants or Third Party contractors, SFJ must instead procure for PB a "worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers" (11.1.1.3(b)-(c)) — i.e. irrevocable in substance, transferable to successors, and extendable to our Affiliates and contractors through the sublicence right. That meets or exceeds the preferred position, so no redline is warranted. The only grant in the other direction (11.1.1.6 "No Other Rights") is protective of us, limiting SFJ to what is necessary to perform, and the Program Transfer licence/transfer mechanics sit in the Exhibit O form outside this text. We note for the record that the contractor licences are obtained on a commercially reasonable efforts basis with an express carve-out in 11.1.1.3(c) for contractor background/improvement technology, and that AZ License and Existing Licenses terms prevail over conflicting grants — sub-elements we would track commercially rather than flag under this rule.
